teachingBodiesReviewedAndCorrected.heading: Treat and grade response
teachingBodiesReviewedAndCorrected.before: Initial Lyme arthritis receives 28 days of oral doxycycline, amoxicillin, or cefuroxime. Partial improvement can be observed or receive a second oral course. Minimal response can receive IV ceftriaxone for 14 to 28 days after reassessment.
teachingBodiesReviewedAndCorrected.after: Initial Lyme arthritis receives 28 days of oral therapy. For mild residual swelling after the first oral course, evidence does not establish observation versus a second course; reassess adherence, other causes, joint findings, and patient preferences. No or minimal response can warrant 2 to 4 weeks of IV ceftriaxone after reassessment.
teachingBodiesReviewedAndCorrected.source: IDSA2020 XXIII and XXIV; partial-response knowledge gap and oral-plus-IV failure boundary; weak/very-low certainty referral

teachingBodiesReviewedAndCorrected.heading: Stop antibiotics after adequate oral and IV care
teachingBodiesReviewedAndCorrected.before: Persistent synovitis after an adequate oral course and an adequate IV course is managed as postantibiotic inflammatory arthritis with rheumatology, not repeated antimicrobial cycles.
teachingBodiesReviewedAndCorrected.after: After failure of one oral antibiotic course and one IV course, the guideline suggests rheumatology or another trained specialist for consideration of DMARDs, biologic agents, intraarticular steroids, or synovectomy. This is a weak recommendation with very low-quality evidence. It is distinct from residual swelling after the first oral course.
teachingBodiesReviewedAndCorrected.source: IDSA2020 XXIII and XXIV; partial-response knowledge gap and oral-plus-IV failure boundary; weak/very-low certainty referral
